ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider (as a Ryde voucher per NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde review for a false "I'm Here" tap made 600 m from the pickup point.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled trip with a $6.61 no-show fee, so it enters the policy through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver's stated reason is rider no-show, which routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 [F3][F6][RD-0, NS-0]. Both advocates read the record the same way, and so do I.

NS-1 requires three cumulative conditions. (i) an arrival confirmation exists — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 [F5][NS-1]. (ii) at the moment of that confirmation the driver must be within the pickup radius (200 m, data-layer parameter G2) — the tap was made 600 m from the pickup, and the driver's closest approach for the whole trip was 599 m at 12:06:55 [F5][F1][NS-1]. (iii) he must then wait at the pickup continuously for more than 3 minutes — he spent 0 s inside the radius after the tap, and his only stationary period (12:05:55–12:09:25, 3 min 30 s) was spent 600 m away, followed by cancellation at 12:09:25 [F5][F2][F3][NS-1]. Conditions (ii) and (iii) both fail, so the no-show fee is not established.

The driver's written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup [F12] is a claim contradicted by the GPS and timeline records in F1, F2, F4 and F5 — system records outrank statements — and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all (driver_arrived_at null) [F4][F12][NS-1]. Nothing external excuses the stand-off: no traffic incidents on the route and fair weather, with only moderate band-3 flow (20–29 km/h) on Jalan Besar, which supports nothing under RD-4's "reasonable cause" branch [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

NS-2 therefore applies: since NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full [F6][F3][NS-2]. The amount is the cancellation fee actually charged, $6.61, and no other published add-on exists — no surge (1.0×) and no toll/ERP component in this dataset [F6][F7][FARE-1, NS-7].

NS-2 also attaches an account consequence where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius: the tap at 600 m with 0 s inside the radius afterwards engages the false-arrival limb, an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button [F5][F1][F2][NS-2]. The driver's 90-day record (1 dispute, 1 upheld, no-show) is an additional-action consideration only and cannot itself decide the case [F17][RD-6, NS-2].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages (driver's 12:06 "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out"; rider's 12:07 "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?"; driver's 12:09 "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel"), the driver's post-trip statement and the complaint [F8][F9][F10][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them — the exchange is a disputed-arrival argument only — so safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1, SAFE-2].

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — full GPS coverage of the wait, the ticketed tap distance, the stationary window, the cancellation time and the fee, with a complete fully timestamped chat (3 messages) [F1][F2][F3][F5][F6][F11]. Nothing needed is missing, so evidence_status is sufficient and no G12 escalation is required; the rider's own presence does not need to be proved, since NS-2 places the burden of the NS-1 conditions on the driver's arrival record.

rejected_claims.reason: The submission that the profile facts (F17: 2295 days' tenure, 4.67 rating, 464 trips in 90 days, 1 upheld no-show dispute) should be weighed so as to neutralise the outcome is rejected: profile facts never decide a case, and the finding already stands on the system records F1, F2, F4 and F5 under NS-1/NS-2 [F17][F5].

The submission that the tap 600 m out and the 600 m stationary period (F5, F2) do not fall within the abuse-of-arrival-button limb is rejected: NS-2 attaches flag_account precisely where the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius, which is what F5 and F1 show [F5][F1][NS-2].

The driver-side gloss that the 12:06 announcement of a silver Toyota Altis (F8) means the rider could have located the car is rejected as a reading of the words: F8 asserts 'I'm here already' while F1, F2 and F5 put the car 599–600 m from the pickup, so the message is contradicted by the system records and cannot evidence a valid arrival [F8][F1][F5][NS-1].

Even taking the driver advocate's own concession, the claim that the 3 min 30 s stationary period (F2) shows a compliant wait is rejected: that period was spent 600 m from the pickup with 0 s inside the radius, so NS-1 (iii) fails [F2][F5][NS-1].

The claim that the driver's 90-day profile (F17, 1 upheld no-show dispute) supports the account flag is rejected in that form: the flag rests on the failed arrival conditions in F5/F1, and F17 is only an additional-action consideration that cannot itself establish the case [F17][F5][NS-2, RD-6].

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
